## Natural history notes

A medium-sized rhinoceros beetle characterized by a smooth oval body, dark brown to black coloration, strong digging legs, and a glossy, somewhat flattened appearance. In Florida, the Rice Beetle is found in fields, pastures, gardens, lawns, wetlands, agricultural areas, and other open habitats with moist soil and decaying organic material. Adults may come to lights and feed on roots or underground plant parts, while the larvae live in soil and feed on roots and decomposing plant material, sometimes becoming minor pests in crops, turf, or pasture systems.
